actions/*.basis: GitHub publishes the Actions platform every repository already runs on, so a non-major release adds no new trust.

github/*.basis: GitHub owns the platform these actions run on; its codeql-action publishes immutable releases.

anthropics/*.basis: Anthropic publishes the review agents every repository trusts; claude-code-action also pulls oven-sh/setup-bun (SHA-pinned) and installs bun packages and the Claude Code CLI at runtime, so this tier trusts those transitively.

reviewOnly.basis: The sync engine parses every manifest with yaml inside the credentialed sync job, so a parser change reaches every consumer.

The only root package with an install script; .github/workflows/eval-browser-dispatch.yml installs the root lockfile and runs its claude CLI with the lane's OAuth token in the step env, and .github/dependabot.yml exempts it from the cooldown, so a hijacked release reaches that token the day it publishes.

.github/workflows/eval-browser-dispatch.yml installs the root lockfile in the job that holds the lane's OAuth token, runs the playwright it pulls in and playwright-cli, and makes Bash(playwright-cli *) the eval's default tool, so it runs beside the claude process holding that token.

.github/actions/resolve-config/action.yml:159 installs this lockfile and :160 runs resolve-config.mjs, whose resolve.mjs:7 loads ajv to validate the lane rules inside credentialed CI lanes; in pr-merge.yml:210-215 its output sets the permissions the lane token is minted with at :261, so a hijacked release can widen that token.
